This is a remote position.

About the Company
Partnerships are the future of go-to-market. They drive 30-50% of company revenue, yet most partner teams are stuck with spreadsheets, email chains, and outdated CRMs built for a different era. The result? Wasted time, lost deals, and inefficiencies that kill growth.
Euler is the AI-native PRM for modern partnership teams, built to replace manual work, eliminate partner friction, and turn partner activity into repeatable revenue and measurable ROI. Our mission: make partner revenue scalable and predictable.
We grew 600% YoY in 2025 and serve industry leaders like Anthropic, Starlink, Gong, and BambooHR. We move fast, build intentionally, and focus on delivering real value.
Role Overview
We are hiring a Director of Marketing who can do three things well: think strategically, make smart decisions quickly, and execute without hand-holding.
This is not a role for someone who produces strategy decks and waits for alignment. It's for someone who formulates a hypothesis, runs the experiment, looks at the data, and moves. You will own the marketing function end-to-end, reporting directly to the CEO, with a clear mandate to drive revenue growth through demand generation and inbound pipeline.
We have real assets already in place: an active newsletter, a growing podcast, strong founder-led thought leadership, a rising G2 presence, active event sponsorships, and engaged communities. Your job is to assess what's working, prioritize the biggest opportunities, and take us in new directions. If after six months we're only doing the things already on this list, we've failed.
You will also work closely with a product marketer who will be joining around the same time and reporting to you, owning product messaging, case studies, and sales enablement materials.
Main Responsibilities
We have invested time and resources into building a variety of marketing channels and initiatives. We're looking for someone to come in, identify where the biggest revenue growth opportunities are, and place the right bets. Here is what exists today:
  • Demand generation strategy and execution across content, email, social, and paid
  • LinkedIn presence and distribution as our primary inbound channel
  • Newsletter, podcast, blog, YouTube, and G2 programs
  • Event sponsorships and partnership community engagement
  • Website copy and landing pages
  • Core messaging and positioning, developed in close partnership with the CEO
  • Marketing metrics tied directly to MQLs, SQLs, pipeline, and revenue
  • Developing and executing enterprise-focused GTM motions, including messaging and positioning for complex, multi-stakeholder buying processes

Requirements

  • 5+ years of B2B SaaS marketing experience, with at least 2 years owning a marketing function
  • B2B SaaS experience selling specifically to other software companies (workflow software, revtech, sales/marketing tech preferred). Experience in industries with non-software buyers (e.g., healthcare, education, government, industrial/regulated sectors) is not a fit for this role, regardless of company size or SaaS maturity
  • Enterprise sales cycle experience is non-negotiable — demonstrated experience marketing to enterprise buyers, including long sales cycles, high ACV deals, and multi-stakeholder buying committees. Experience limited to SMB or early-stage/self-serve motions does not meet the bar for this role
  • Demand generation focus with a track record of driving qualified pipeline and measurable revenue impact, not just awareness
  • Comfortable owning a revenue number and being held accountable to it
  • Experience in or exposure to partner marketing or partnerships-led growth. Understanding this space is a meaningful advantage and shortens the learning curve significantly
  • Scrappy and execution-oriented. You build channels from the ground up, not from a template
  • Strong critical thinking and judgment about which bets are worth making and which aren't
  • Exceptional writing skills. You can translate complex product capabilities into narratives that land with the right buyer
  • Senior enough to manage a team, but not above rolling up your sleeves and doing the work yourself before one exists
  • Portfolio required: include examples of content you've produced and programs you've built or scaled
Nice to Have
  • Experience in PRM, CRM, or partner-led growth platforms
  • Familiarity with HubSpot for marketing operations
  • Experience managing or mentoring junior marketing team members
Why Join
  • A marketing function with real traction already in place. You prioritize and build on it, not from scratch
  • Direct line to the CEO. Your strategy shapes how the product shows up in the market
  • A product marketer joining alongside you to own the product messaging layer, freeing you to focus on growth
  • The kind of place where you write the playbook, not follow one
We grew 600% last year with virtually no formal marketing function, and are already on track to grow 300% this year. What the right person can do with what we've already built is a wide open question. If you've ever wanted to step into a role where the ceiling is genuinely undefined, where the work you do in the next 12 months could meaningfully change the trajectory of a company and your career, this is that opportunity. The foundation is here. The momentum is real. We're looking for the person who knows exactly what to do with it.
If this sounds like you, we'd love to meet you.

Benefits

  • Compensation: USD $120k–$175k annually
  • Work Location:Remote (Must accommodate US East Coast working hours)

Operations Lead

Remote | Full-time | 40-hours/week
Rate: $6 to $7/hour, with the final rate to be determined during the final interview.

About Pillar Health Solutions ()

Pillar Health Solutions partners with medical practices to provide outsourced nutrition, dietary, exercise, and wellness support to their patients.

Our model allows physician practices to expand the services available to their patients without having to build and manage an entire wellness team internally. Pillar supports the operational infrastructure behind the program, including patient coordination, provider support, scheduling, documentation, communication, reporting, and billing-related workflows.

We are building a model that should feel simple and seamless for the physician practice, even though there are many moving parts behind the scenes.

That is where the Operations Lead comes in.

About the Role

We are looking for an Operations Lead who can build, run, and continuously improve the operational engine behind Pillar Health Solutions.

This is a highly hands-on role for someone who is comfortable working in a growing healthcare business where processes are still evolving.

You will work closely with leadership and take ownership of the workflows connecting physician partners, practice staff, patients, dietitians, exercise professionals, and internal support teams.

You may be investigating why patients are not scheduling, improving a referral workflow, resolving a practice issue, reviewing operational data, building a new process, creating an SOP, coordinating provider capacity, or implementing automation to eliminate repetitive work.

As Pillar grows, this role should evolve from personally managing many operational processes to building the systems, team structure, accountability, and workflows that allow the company to scale efficiently.

We are looking for someone who does not simply identify problems. You should be able to determine why they are happening, create a practical solution, implement it, and measure whether the solution worked.

What You Will Own

Practice Onboarding & Client Operations

  • Own new practice onboarding from agreement through launch, including referral, scheduling, communication, documentation, and billing-related workflows.

  • Serve as a key operational point of contact for physician partners and practice staff, ensuring requests, concerns, and follow-ups are addressed promptly.

Patient Operations & Engagement

  • Oversee the patient journey from referral through outreach, scheduling, first appointment, and ongoing engagement.

  • Monitor cancellations, no-shows, scheduling delays, and patient drop-off points, then implement workflows to improve conversion and retention.

Provider & Clinical Operations

  • Coordinate operationally with dietitians, exercise professionals, and support staff to maintain appropriate availability, capacity, and coverage.

  • Monitor provider scheduling, patient assignments, operational responsiveness, and adherence to documentation expectations.

Documentation, Billing & Revenue Operations

  • Monitor the timely completion and flow of documentation and billing-related information between providers, Pillar, and partner practices.

  • Investigate operational issues that may delay billing, reimbursement, or revenue and coordinate appropriate resolution.

Systems, SOPs & Process Improvement

  • Map workflows, identify bottlenecks, duplicated work, and failure points, then redesign processes to improve speed, accuracy, and accountability.

  • Build practical SOPs, trackers, dashboards, templates, checklists, and standardized workflows for recurring operational activities.

KPI & Performance Management

  • Track core operational KPIs across referrals, scheduling, patient engagement, provider utilization, documentation, service delivery, and partner performance.

  • Analyze trends and operational gaps to determine what changed, why it changed, and what action should be taken.

  • Provide leadership with concise reporting on performance, risks, unresolved issues, priorities, and recommended next steps.

Technology & AI

  • Evaluate and implement tools that simplify operations, reduce administrative workload, and improve visibility across the business.

  • Use AI and automation to improve reporting, workflow management, analysis, documentation, communication, and recurring operational processes.

Founder & Leadership Partnership

  • Translate leadership priorities and ideas into clear operational plans, owners, timelines, and measurable outcomes.

  • Surface risks and unresolved issues early while bringing recommended solutions instead of only reporting problems.

What We Are Looking For

Required Qualifications

  • 2+ years of experience in healthcare operations, medical practice operations, program management, client success, healthcare administration, or a closely related field.

  • Experience owning processes and outcomes rather than only completing assigned administrative tasks.

  • Strong understanding of patient scheduling, provider coordination, documentation, healthcare administrative workflows, and service operations.

  • Demonstrated ability to identify operational problems, investigate root causes, and independently implement solutions.

  • Strong organizational, analytical, and problem-solving skills.

  • Excellent written and spoken English.

  • Strong communication skills and confidence interacting with physicians, practice staff, healthcare professionals, patients, and senior leadership.

  • Experience creating or improving SOPs, workflows, dashboards, trackers, or operational systems.

  • Strong attention to detail, particularly when working with patient information, documentation, billing information, and operational data.

  • Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-moving, changing, or early-stage environment.

  • Comfortable learning unfamiliar tools, systems, workflows, and processes independently.

  • Practical experience using AI, automation, or technology to improve business processes.

Highly Preferred

  • Experience supporting US medical practices or healthcare organizations.

  • Experience in telehealth, nutrition, wellness, chronic care, preventive health, exercise programs, or virtual healthcare services.

  • Familiarity with healthcare insurance, eligibility, reimbursement, billing, claims, or revenue-cycle workflows.

  • Experience working with EHR/EMR systems, scheduling platforms, CRM tools, telehealth systems, or patient communication platforms.

  • Experience coordinating or managing remote healthcare teams.

  • Experience with physician practice onboarding, account management, or client success.

  • Experience building processes or operations within an early-stage or rapidly growing company.

  • Previous ownership of operational KPIs, service-level metrics, or business performance reporting.

The Type of Person Who Will Succeed Here

You are someone who naturally asks:

What is supposed to happen? What is actually happening? Where is the gap? Why is it happening? Who owns fixing it? How do we prevent it from happening again?

You are proactive, resourceful, highly organized, and comfortable working with ambiguity.

You do not need every process to already exist before you can start working. You are comfortable creating structure where structure is missing.

You enjoy both strategy and execution. You can discuss operational priorities with leadership and then personally investigate a scheduling issue, analyze a broken workflow, create a process, or coordinate a solution.

You are comfortable taking ownership without waiting to be repeatedly reminded.

You communicate clearly, escalate thoughtfully, and understand the difference between simply reporting a problem and actually helping solve it.

Most importantly, you think in terms of systems.

When the same issue happens repeatedly, your instinct should not be to keep fixing it manually. Your instinct should be to understand why it keeps happening and build a better process.

What Success Looks Like

During your first few weeks, success will mean developing a strong understanding of Pillar's end-to-end operating model and creating clear visibility into how physician practices, patients, providers, documentation, billing, and internal workflows connect.

You will identify the biggest operational bottlenecks, improve patient and practice workflows, strengthen accountability, establish meaningful operational reporting, and reduce recurring operational issues.

Over time, you will help build an operating system capable of supporting substantially more physician practices, patients, and providers without operational complexity increasing at the same rate as the business.

The ultimate goal is simple:

Create an operation where physician practices receive a reliable experience, patients move through the program smoothly, providers have the support they need, leadership has visibility into performance, and fewer problems require manual intervention as Pillar grows.

POSITION SUMMARY


The Client & Customer Experience (C&CE) organization is responsible for the servicing of Cigna customers across multiple lines of business. Within C&CE, the Learning & Knowledge Management arm of Operational Excellence supports the capabilities, tools, and information employees need to serve customers accurately and effectively.

The Business Analytics Advisor works within an analytics team that supports Learning & Knowledge Management by delivering high-quality analytics, trusted data, and lightweight digital solutions. In this role, the Business Analytics Advisor works from priorities and requirements established by the Product Owner, then translates those needs into reliable datasets, analyses, reporting solutions, and digital tools. The role partners closely with Learning, Knowledge Management, Operational Excellence, Operations, and technology teams to improve learner readiness, knowledge effectiveness, and operational performance.

This is a fully remote opportunity for candidates in select geographies. Candidates who reside within 50 miles of the following locations will be required to perform onsite 3 days per week: Bloomfield, CT; Chattanooga, TN; Denver, CO; Scottsdale, AZ.; St. Louis, MO.

raw.title: Subscription Pricing & Strategy Director
raw.excerpt: GoodRx is the leading prescription savings platform in the U.
raw.description:
GoodRx is the leading prescription savings platform in the U.S.Trusted by more than 25 million consumers and 750,000 healthcare professionals annually, GoodRx provides access to savings and affordability options for generic and brand-name medications at more than 70,000 pharmacies nationwide, as well as comprehensive healthcare research and information. Since 2011, GoodRx has helped consumers save nearly $75 billion on the cost of their prescriptions.

Our goal is to help Americans find convenient and affordable healthcare. We offer solutions for consumers, employers, health plans, and anyone else who shares our desire to provide affordable prescriptions to all Americans.

About the Role:

We are seeking a highly analytical and strategic Subscription Pricing & Strategy Director to shape the growth strategy and economics of GoodRx’s consumer subscription business. This role will serve as a senior strategic leader at the intersection of subscription strategy, pricing, analytics, and product, defining opportunities and influencing decisions across acquisition, engagement, retention, monetization, and long-term customer value.


The Director will be expected to develop an enterprise-level perspective on the subscription business, identify the highest-value opportunities, and establish the analytical and strategic frameworks used to evaluate them. This role will tackle complex, often ambiguous business questions where the path forward is not predefined, using customer, behavioral, financial, and market insights to develop clear points of view and guide investment and product decisions.


Working closely with senior leaders across Product, Pricing, Finance, Analytics, Marketing, and Design, this individual will influence strategy and priorities, challenge assumptions, and translate insights into coordinated action. The Director will operate with significant autonomy and will be accountable for both the quality of strategic recommendations and their impact on business outcomes.


The ideal candidate combines exceptional analytical depth with strong commercial judgment and executive-level communication. They can move fluidly between long-range strategy and detailed analysis, recognize patterns and implications beyond the immediate question, and influence decisions across organizational boundaries. Experience in subscription businesses, pricing, consumer technology, or consumer health technology is highly valued.


Responsibilities:

  • Set subscription growth and economic strategy: Develop and continuously refine strategies to accelerate subscriber growth, engagement, retention, lifetime value, and profitability. Identify structural opportunities and risks and establish clear recommendations and priorities for senior leadership.
  • Shape pricing and monetization strategy: Partner with Pricing, Product, Finance, and Analytics leaders to define approaches to subscription pricing, packaging, promotions, benefits, and monetization. Evaluate customer response, competitive dynamics, willingness to pay, and unit economics to inform major pricing decisions.
  • Lead high-impact strategic analyses: Independently frame and solve complex, ambiguous business problems using behavioral, financial, customer, and market data. Develop hypotheses, determine appropriate analytical approaches, synthesize findings, and translate them into consequential business recommendations.
  • Identify and prioritize growth opportunities: Proactively identify opportunities across the subscription lifecycle and determine where GoodRx should invest. Size opportunities, evaluate strategic and economic tradeoffs, build business cases, and establish decision criteria and success measures.
  • Own the strategic view of subscription performance: Develop a holistic perspective on the drivers of acquisition, conversion, engagement, retention, revenue, lifetime value, and margin. Identify emerging trends, underlying drivers, and implications that require leadership attention or changes in strategy.
  • Influence product and business priorities: Translate customer and economic insights into recommendations that shape product roadmaps, investment decisions, benefit design, go-to-market strategies, and experimentation priorities.
  • Drive cross-functional decision-making: Lead complex initiatives spanning Product, Pricing, Finance, Marketing, Design, Analytics, and other teams. Create alignment among stakeholders with differing objectives and drive decisions forward when ownership, data, or the path to resolution is ambiguous.
  • Advise senior leadership: Serve as a trusted strategic thought partner to senior leaders on subscription growth, pricing, monetization, and economics. Develop concise, executive-ready narratives that synthesize complex analyses, articulate tradeoffs, and recommend a clear course of action.
  • Establish scalable decision frameworks: Build and institutionalize analytical models, strategic frameworks, measurement approaches, and operating mechanisms that improve the quality and speed of subscription-related decisions across the organization.
  • Raise the analytical and strategic bar: Establish best practices for problem structuring, business-case development, experimentation, and strategic analysis. Provide thought leadership and mentorship to colleagues and cross-functional partners without requiring direct people-management responsibility.

Skills & Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree required; Master’s degree strongly preferred.
  • 12+ years of progressive experience in strategy, pricing, analytics, management consulting, corporate strategy, product strategy, monetization, or related disciplines, including experience leading complex, high-impact business decisions.
  • Experience in subscription strategy, pricing, packaging, monetization, or revenue management
  • Demonstrated ability to independently define and solve highly ambiguous problems, establish a strategic point of view, and influence decisions with significant business and financial implications.
  • Deep expertise in using quantitative and qualitative insights to understand customer behavior, business performance, and economic drivers.
  • Strong commercial and financial acumen, including experience evaluating unit economics, customer lifetime value, investment tradeoffs, and business cases.
  • Advanced SQL, Excel, and PowerPoint capabilities; experience with Python, R, or similar analytical tools is a plus.
  • Demonstrated ability to move beyond reporting and analysis to identify second-order implications, structural opportunities, and strategic risks.
  • Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with demonstrated ability to distill complex issues into clear recommendations for executive audiences.
  • Strong executive presence and ability to influence senior stakeholders and drive alignment across teams without relying on formal authority.
  • Proven ability to operate with significant autonomy, exercise sound judgment with incomplete information, and simultaneously navigate strategic and executional complexity.

Experience That Is Especially Valuable:

  • Consumer technology or consumer health technology / healthcare
  • Subscription unit economics, lifetime value, churn, and retention optimization
  • Experimentation, customer behavior analytics, segmentation, or willingness-to-pay analysis
  • Product strategy and experience influencing product roadmaps and investment decisions

Offre d'emploi : Directeur de la Génération de Preuves

Mission Principale : Concevoir et fournir les preuves cliniques du monde réel nécessaires pour obtenir l'approbation réglementaire, le remboursement et l'adoption sur le marché pour les logiciels en tant que dispositif médical. Ce rôle se situe à l'intersection du développement clinique, de la réglementation, des preuves du monde réel, de l'HEOR et de la science des données/santé numérique. Le poste relève du VP du Développement Clinique & des Affaires Médicales.

Activités Principales :

  • Conception d'Études Cliniques & du Monde Réel

    • Concevoir et superviser des essais cliniques (essais pragmatiques, interventionnels)

    • Conduire des études observationnelles (études de cohorte, registres)

    • Utiliser des études de données du monde réel en utilisant des données générées par des dispositifs et des données de réclamations

    • Garantir des méthodologies adaptées pour la santé numérique (conceptions adaptatives, bras de contrôle externes)

  • Preuves du Monde Réel & Stratégie Post-Marché

    • Aligner la stratégie de preuve avec les voies réglementaires et décider des conceptions d'étude & des critères d'évaluation

    • Élaborer des plans de preuves post-marché : PMCF, gestion du cycle de vie de l'IA

    • Tirer parti des flux de données numériques (données d'utilisation du produit, registres, biomarqueurs numériques)

  • HEOR & Démonstration de la Valeur

    • Garantir des rapports de preuves

    • Collaborer avec les organismes d'évaluation des technologies de la santé

  • Leadership Interfonctionnel

    • Agir en tant qu'intégrateur stratégique à travers les fonctions :

      • Développement clinique

      • Biostatistique

      • Science des données / IA

      • Affaires médicales

      • Affaires réglementaires

      • Accès au marché/commercial

  • Partenariats Externes

    • Collaborer avec les réseaux hospitaliers, les centres académiques, les CRO et les centres de données/registres

Requirements

Compétences Clés

  • Technique

    • Épidémiologie clinique, biostatistique

    • Méthodologie RWE

    • Cadres réglementaires (FDA, EU MDR, directives IMDRF SaMD)

    • Cadres de validation de la santé numérique / IA

  • Stratégique

    • Pensée du cycle de vie

    • Compréhension des attentes des payeurs

    • Planification des preuves alignée sur les objectifs commerciaux

  • Opérationnel

    • Supervision de l'exécution des études

    • Gestion des fournisseurs

    • Contrôle du budget & des délais

  • Leadership

    • Traduire des données complexes en décisions

    • Raconter des histoires avec des preuves

    • Compétences d'influence

    • Excellentes capacités de communication et de leadership

    • Favoriser une culture d'innovation

Livrables Typiques

  • Plan de Preuves Intégré/plans de preuves PM

  • Contribuer à CEP/CER

  • Protocoles d'étude

  • Modèles HEOR

  • Publications

Parcours

  • MD, PharmD ou PhD ou équivalent (Diplôme avancé en sciences de la vie)

  • >10 ans en Épidémiologie, RWE, HEOR/économie médicale

  • Leadership éprouvé dans l'environnement pharmaceutique/biotechnologique ou CRO

  • Expérience antérieure dans les technologies médicales ou la santé numérique

    Median Technologies s'engage en faveur de la diversité culturelle, de l'égalité des genres et de l'emploi des travailleurs handicapés.

raw.excerpt: ABOUT GREYSTAR Greystar is a leading, fully integrated global real estate platform offering expertise in property management, investment management, development, and construction services in institutional-quality rental housing.
raw.description:
ABOUT GREYSTAR


Greystar is a leading, fully integrated global real estate platform offering expertise in property management, investment management, development, and construction services in institutional-quality rental housing. Headquartered in Charleston, South Carolina, Greystar manages and operates over $350 billion of real estate in more than 260 markets globally with offices throughout North America, Europe, South America, and the Asia-Pacific region. Greystar is the largest operator of apartments in the United States, managing over one million units/beds globally. Across its platforms, Greystar has nearly $79 billion of assets under management, including over $34 billion of development assets and over $36.5 billion of regulatory assets under management. Greystar was founded by Bob Faith in 1993 to become a provider of world-class service in the rental residential real estate business. To learn more, visit .

JOB DESCRIPTION SUMMARY

Greystar is seeking an experienced, highly technical, hands-on, and mission-driven Technical Program Manager (TPM) to lead engineering initiatives within our Digital, Data & AI team. The TPM will have a strong sense of ownership, aid in identifying and resolving dependencies, track progress across different teams, and ensure the work progresses, while clearly communicating progress and risks to project stakeholders.

This role sits at the delivery core of the Data Digital and AI team and is distinct from our Product Managers/Owners: PMs own the what and why (product direction and roadmap priorities); the TPM owns the how and when, driving execution end-to-end across engineering teams without absorbing product scope.

Success in this role requires an equal blend of hands-on technical fluency and strong project and program management discipline. Nearly every initiative brings together multiple engineering disciplines within a single project — data engineering, application/product engineering (web and mobile), and infrastructure.

JOB DESCRIPTION

JOB DESCRIPTION

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Own end-to-end delivery for assigned initiatives, from scoping through launch, driving progress across data engineering, product engineering (web and mobile), and infrastructure teams, often within the same project.
  • Partner with Product Managers to translate product strategy and roadmaps into executable delivery plans. Product Managers own product direction; TPMs own sequencing, dependencies, and delivery risk.
  • Drive delivery for application-centric initiatives, including web and mobile feature launches, API/service integrations, and release coordination — with enough fluency in app architecture to pressure-test estimates, identify technical debt risk, and sequence frontend/backend/mobile workstreams realistically.
  • Keep initiatives moving under competing priorities by driving stalled decisions to resolution with clear options, a recommended default, and a named owner, rather than allowing work to drift.
  • Regularly assess risks and opportunities; understand best practices, drive process improvements, and find new ways of operating, with a focus on simplification and productivity.
  • Run the delivery operating system in Linear, including sprint planning, dependency tracking, RACI, and status reporting, as the single source of truth across multiple product teams.
  • Drive initiatives with a heavy data component, coordinating data readiness, integration, and quality across delivery, with enough fluency to pressure-test estimates and ensure data-dependent plans are realistic.

BASIC KNOWLEDGE & QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Proven track record of managing large-scale, complex technical initiatives for product development & software engineering with clear evidence of technical delivery you personally owned and shaped.
  • Demonstrated ability to work through ambiguity to detailed solutions. You can take a vague problem, crisply frame the challenge, identify a path forward, and drive an initiative over the finish line.
  • Self-motivated, proactive, and proven ability to adapt well and work with teams having different operating cadences.
  • Strong working knowledge of data, including the ability to read a data model, understand pipeline and integration dependencies, assess data quality, and hold teams accountable for data readiness. This is not a data engineering role, but you must be able to identify and address data-related risks.
  • Strong working knowledge of application development, including the ability to read a system/architecture diagram, understand client-server and API dependencies, assess technical debt and scalability tradeoffs, and hold teams accountable for release readiness. This is not a software engineering role, but you must be able to identify and address app-delivery risks
  • Experience developing processes where little exists and demonstrated flexibility to get things done.
  • Proven experience leading delivery across multiple engineering disciplines, not just one. You have coordinated data engineering, product or application engineering (web and/or mobile), and infrastructure within the same initiative.
  • Detail-oriented and able to understand the bigger picture by using your technical expertise and problem-solving abilities to prioritize and manage blocking issues.
  • Experience working in a highly cross-functional environment where communication with multiple groups is imperative.
  • Ability to build working knowledge quickly across unfamiliar technical areas. You will move between data, application, and infrastructure work and must understand each well enough to lead delivery and challenge engineering estimates.
  • Ability to ramp up quickly and learn new technologies with minimal lag time.
  • Excellent written and oral business communication and people skills, with the ability to influence stakeholders.
  • Experience with the Linear project management system or similar (Jira, Asana, etc).

The salary range for this position is $115,000 - $140,000 USD Annually.


Additional Compensation:


Many factors go into determining employee pay within the posted range including business requirements, prior experience, current skills and geographical location.

  • Corporate Positions: In addition to the base salary, this role may be eligible to participate in a quarterly or annual bonus program based on individual and company performance.
  • Onsite Property Positions: In addition to the base salary, this role may be eligible to participate in weekly, monthly, and/or quarterly bonus programs.

Robust Benefits Offered*:

  • Competitive Medical, Dental, Vision, and Disability & Life insurance benefits. Low (free basic) employee Medical costs for employee-only coverage; costs discounted after 3 and 5 years of service.
  • Generous Paid Time off. All new hires start with 15 days of vacation, 4 personal days, 10 sick days, and 11 paid holidays. Plus your birthday off after 1 year of service! Additional vacation accrued with tenure.
  • For onsite team members, onsite housing discount at Greystar-managed communities are available subject to discount and unit availability.
  • 6-Week Paid Sabbatical after 10 years of service (and every 5 years thereafter).
  • 401(k) with Company Match up to 6% of pay after 6 months of service.
  • Paid Parental Leave and lifetime Fertility Benefit reimbursement up to $10,000 (includes adoption or surrogacy).
  • Employee Assistance Program.
  • Critical Illness, Accident, Hospital Indemnity, Pet Insurance and Legal Plans.
  • Charitable giving program and benefits.

*Benefits offered for full-time employees. For Union and Prevailing Wage roles, compensation and benefits may vary from the listed information above due to Collective Bargaining Agreements and/or local governing authority.


Greystar will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.


Greystar is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate in employment on the basis of race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy, sexual orientation, and gender identity), national origin, age, disability, genetic information, military or veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.


This position may be performed remotely anywhere within the United States except the state of Alaska.


Important Notice: Greystar will never request your banking details or other sensitive personal information during the interview process. Greystar does not conduct any interviews via text or messaging, and all communication will come from official Greystar email addresses (@greystar.com). If you receive suspicious requests, please report them immediately to .

raw.description:
ABOUT GREYSTAR


Greystar is a leading, fully integrated global real estate platform offering expertise in property management, investment management, development, and construction services in institutional-quality rental housing. Headquartered in Charleston, South Carolina, Greystar manages and operates over $350 billion of real estate in more than 260 markets globally with offices throughout North America, Europe, South America, and the Asia-Pacific region. Greystar is the largest operator of apartments in the United States, managing over one million units/beds globally. Across its platforms, Greystar has nearly $79 billion of assets under management, including over $34 billion of development assets and over $36.5 billion of regulatory assets under management. Greystar was founded by Bob Faith in 1993 to become a provider of world-class service in the rental residential real estate business. To learn more, visit .

JOB DESCRIPTION SUMMARY

Greystar is seeking an experienced, highly technical, hands-on, and mission-driven Technical Program Manager (TPM) to lead engineering initiatives within our Digital, Data & AI team. The TPM will have a strong sense of ownership, aid in identifying and resolving dependencies, track progress across different teams, and ensure the work progresses, while clearly communicating progress and risks to project stakeholders.

This role sits at the delivery core of the Data Digital and AI team and is distinct from our Product Managers/Owners: PMs own the what and why (product direction and roadmap priorities); the TPM owns the how and when, driving execution end-to-end across engineering teams without absorbing product scope.

Success in this role requires an equal blend of hands-on technical fluency and strong project and program management discipline. Nearly every initiative brings together multiple engineering disciplines within a single project — data engineering, application/product engineering (web and mobile), and infrastructure.

JOB DESCRIPTION

JOB DESCRIPTION

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Own end-to-end delivery for assigned initiatives, from scoping through launch, driving progress across data engineering, product engineering (web and mobile), and infrastructure teams, often within the same project.
  • Partner with Product Managers to translate product strategy and roadmaps into executable delivery plans. Product Managers own product direction; TPMs own sequencing, dependencies, and delivery risk.
  • Drive delivery for application-centric initiatives, including web and mobile feature launches, API/service integrations, and release coordination — with enough fluency in app architecture to pressure-test estimates, identify technical debt risk, and sequence frontend/backend/mobile workstreams realistically.
  • Keep initiatives moving under competing priorities by driving stalled decisions to resolution with clear options, a recommended default, and a named owner, rather than allowing work to drift.
  • Regularly assess risks and opportunities; understand best practices, drive process improvements, and find new ways of operating, with a focus on simplification and productivity.
  • Run the delivery operating system in Linear, including sprint planning, dependency tracking, RACI, and status reporting, as the single source of truth across multiple product teams.
  • Drive initiatives with a heavy data component, coordinating data readiness, integration, and quality across delivery, with enough fluency to pressure-test estimates and ensure data-dependent plans are realistic.

BASIC KNOWLEDGE & QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Proven track record of managing large-scale, complex technical initiatives for product development & software engineering with clear evidence of technical delivery you personally owned and shaped.
  • Demonstrated ability to work through ambiguity to detailed solutions. You can take a vague problem, crisply frame the challenge, identify a path forward, and drive an initiative over the finish line.
  • Self-motivated, proactive, and proven ability to adapt well and work with teams having different operating cadences.
  • Strong working knowledge of data, including the ability to read a data model, understand pipeline and integration dependencies, assess data quality, and hold teams accountable for data readiness. This is not a data engineering role, but you must be able to identify and address data-related risks.
  • Strong working knowledge of application development, including the ability to read a system/architecture diagram, understand client-server and API dependencies, assess technical debt and scalability tradeoffs, and hold teams accountable for release readiness. This is not a software engineering role, but you must be able to identify and address app-delivery risks
  • Experience developing processes where little exists and demonstrated flexibility to get things done.
  • Proven experience leading delivery across multiple engineering disciplines, not just one. You have coordinated data engineering, product or application engineering (web and/or mobile), and infrastructure within the same initiative.
  • Detail-oriented and able to understand the bigger picture by using your technical expertise and problem-solving abilities to prioritize and manage blocking issues.
  • Experience working in a highly cross-functional environment where communication with multiple groups is imperative.
  • Ability to build working knowledge quickly across unfamiliar technical areas. You will move between data, application, and infrastructure work and must understand each well enough to lead delivery and challenge engineering estimates.
  • Ability to ramp up quickly and learn new technologies with minimal lag time.
  • Excellent written and oral business communication and people skills, with the ability to influence stakeholders.
  • Experience with the Linear project management system or similar (Jira, Asana, etc).

The salary range for this position is $115,000 - $140,000 USD Annually.


Additional Compensation:


Many factors go into determining employee pay within the posted range including business requirements, prior experience, current skills and geographical location.

  • Corporate Positions: In addition to the base salary, this role may be eligible to participate in a quarterly or annual bonus program based on individual and company performance.
  • Onsite Property Positions: In addition to the base salary, this role may be eligible to participate in weekly, monthly, and/or quarterly bonus programs.

Robust Benefits Offered*:

  • Competitive Medical, Dental, Vision, and Disability & Life insurance benefits. Low (free basic) employee Medical costs for employee-only coverage; costs discounted after 3 and 5 years of service.
  • Generous Paid Time off. All new hires start with 15 days of vacation, 4 personal days, 10 sick days, and 11 paid holidays. Plus your birthday off after 1 year of service! Additional vacation accrued with tenure.
  • For onsite team members, onsite housing discount at Greystar-managed communities are available subject to discount and unit availability.
  • 6-Week Paid Sabbatical after 10 years of service (and every 5 years thereafter).
  • 401(k) with Company Match up to 6% of pay after 6 months of service.
  • Paid Parental Leave and lifetime Fertility Benefit reimbursement up to $10,000 (includes adoption or surrogacy).
  • Employee Assistance Program.
  • Critical Illness, Accident, Hospital Indemnity, Pet Insurance and Legal Plans.
  • Charitable giving program and benefits.

*Benefits offered for full-time employees. For Union and Prevailing Wage roles, compensation and benefits may vary from the listed information above due to Collective Bargaining Agreements and/or local governing authority.


Greystar will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.


Greystar is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate in employment on the basis of race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy, sexual orientation, and gender identity), national origin, age, disability, genetic information, military or veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.


This position may be performed remotely anywhere within the United States except the state of Alaska.


Important Notice: Greystar will never request your banking details or other sensitive personal information during the interview process. Greystar does not conduct any interviews via text or messaging, and all communication will come from official Greystar email addresses (@greystar.com). If you receive suspicious requests, please report them immediately to .

raw.description:
Clean & Prosperous Job Opportunity

Clean & Prosperous is seeking an Executive Director to lead our next chapter.

Washington's Climate Commitment Act is one of the most ambitious carbon markets in the world, and one of the most closely watched. We helped build it, helped defend it at the ballot box, and have spent the years since working to make sure it delivers — for emissions, for communities, and for the businesses whose participation the model depends on.

That work has made us something unusual. We are not a typical environmental advocacy organization and we are not a business association. We are a nonpartisan, data-driven organization that businesses, agencies, legislators, Tribal leaders, and environmental groups all trust enough to sit down with. That position took a decade to earn, and it is the foundation of everything we do.

Our next Executive Director will join a skilled team, a diversified revenue base, and a set of ambitions that will require the organization to grow. We are looking for a leader with a track record of building revenue, relationships, and high-performing teams; the entrepreneurial instinct to turn opportunity into results; and the confidence to take on ambitious goals.

Who We Are

Clean & Prosperous is a nonpartisan nonprofit advancing clean energy solutions that grow Washington's economy, improve public health, and reduce carbon emissions. We began in 2013 as an alliance of business leaders who believed that climate policy and economic prosperity are not a trade-off — and that the fastest path to decarbonization runs through practical, evidence-based policy that businesses can support.

We were founded by the late David Giuliani, an entrepreneur best known for co-inventing the Sonicare toothbrush, who spent the final decade of his life bringing together leaders from across sectors and ideologies to pursue pragmatic climate solutions. That entrepreneurial approach still shapes how we work.

We Convene

Study Missions, the Future of Carbon Policy Forum, and cross-sector working groups that bring business, government, Tribal, labor, and environmental leaders together on hard questions.

We Educate

Original research and analysis that translates complex policy into plain language — the Climate Commitment Map, CCA budget and economic analysis, and tools that policymakers, reporters, and businesses use.

We Advocate

Common-sense climate policy in Olympia, grounded in evidence, that holds the state accountable to the commitments made in the CCA.

We Electrify

Direct program delivery accelerating clean transportation — EV charging infrastructure, zero-emission trucks, and fleet electrification across Washington.

What We've Built

We do policy work and we deliver programs. That combination means we are not analyzing the clean energy transition from the outside — we are in it, and what we learn delivering the work shapes what we advocate for. Some of what that has produced:

  • We helped write and pass the Climate Commitment Act, then helped defend it against repeal, and we remain an independent voice on how well it is working.

  • Washington's carbon auctions have raised $4.72 billion, with 50% directed to overburdened communities and 10% to Tribal Nation–led projects. We map and track more than 3,800 funded projects across the state so that the public can see what the policy is buying.

  • Through Charging Forward Together, we are supporting the deployment of more than 5,000 new public EV charging ports in communities across Washington — work that also generates significant earned revenue for the organization.

  • We helped secure $126 million for the Washington Zero-Emission Incentive Program (WAZIP) and are a founding member of the Breaking Barriers Collaborative, which helps school districts and fleet operators electrify.

  • We launched Build SHIIT — Sustainable High-Impact Infrastructure Together — an initiative focused on the bottleneck that increasingly defines climate progress: Washington's inability to permit, site, interconnect, and actually build energy and industrial infrastructure.

  • Our Study Missions have brought Washington policymakers, business leaders, and Tribal leaders to Europe, Canada, California, Texas and Eastern Washington to study energy policies and activities as well as carbon markets firsthand, and our annual Future of Carbon Policy Forum convenes the people shaping this work regionally and nationally.

Why This Moment

Our Washington work matters more than ever

Washington's climate policy is a live experiment that other states, and other countries, are watching. Whether cap-and-invest is judged a success depends on implementation: whether emissions actually fall, whether the revenue is invested well, and whether businesses and communities see the benefit. We are positioned to track that honestly and to convene the people who can fix what isn't working. The political and funding environment is uncertain, which makes independent, credible analysis more valuable, not less.

Our programs are genuinely innovative

Build SHIIT takes on permitting and interconnection — unglamorous work that determines whether any of the state's clean energy goals are achievable. Charging Forward Together puts us in the position of delivering infrastructure, not just recommending it. Our mapping and budget analysis have made the CCA legible to the public. Each of these started as someone's idea about a gap no one else was filling, and each has become both a program and a source of revenue.

The work is beginning to extend beyond Washington

Other states are looking at what happened here, and some of them want help. Policy export — to Minnesota, Pennsylvania, and elsewhere — is a real strategic priority. How far and how fast we go is one of the significant questions our next Executive Director will help answer.

We are at a growth inflection point

Our current annual budget is approximately $1.6 million, and our strategic plan targets meaningful growth over the next three years. Getting there will require the systems, structure, and board development that come with the next stage of an organization's life. For the right leader, that is one of the more interesting parts of the job.

The Team and the Transition

We are twelve people, remote across Washington, with roughly six direct reports to the Executive Director — including our government relations, finance, communications, and research directors, plus two roles to be defined as we redevelop the organization chart. We are governed by a seven-member Board of Directors drawn from business, finance, government affairs, and policy.

Our team describes itself as nimble, ambitious, and low-ego. People here are trusted as experts in their areas and are used to making decisions quickly. We are not looking for a figurehead, and we are not looking for a micromanager. When we asked our staff and board what they most want in the next leader, the same words came back repeatedly: credible, collaborative, decisive, and generous with credit.

Michael Mann has led Clean & Prosperous for five years. He came to us as a contractor, stepped into an interim role, and stayed. He is stepping down at the end of 2026 to focus on his own firm, Cyan Strategies, and other commitments, and he intends to remain a supportive partner to the organization through his firm on specific programs. Our Board is committed to defining that continuing relationship clearly, so that the incoming Executive Director has both full authority and a genuine resource.

What the Executive Director Does

The Executive Director reports to the Board of Directors and holds strategic, financial, external, and organizational leadership of Clean & Prosperous.

Revenue and financial sustainability

Own the funding model. We are working toward a mix of roughly 60% work-product and contract income, 20% event and forum income, and 20% philanthropy — a model built so that the work we do generates the revenue that sustains it. The Executive Director will evaluate that model, sustain and grow contract and funded work, build corporate membership and sponsorship, deepen philanthropic relationships, and manage the organization’s finances with discipline.

External credibility and relationships

In partnership with our communications director and lobbyist, serve as the organization's primary external voice with legislators, agencies, corporate leaders, funders, Tribal partners, labor, environmental organizations, and media. Build and hold the trust that allows us to convene people who do not agree with each other.

Strategic direction and growth

Set priorities with the Board on the questions that matter most: where do we focus, if and when do we pivot on priorities, where do new earned-revenue opportunities exist, how quickly to scale, if and how to pursue policy export beyond Washington, and what we should stop doing.

Policy leadership

Ensure our advocacy is rigorous and effective, working alongside an experienced government relations team, and define the Executive Director's role in Washington's legislative work.

Team leadership and organizational development

Lead and develop a talented, independent staff; build the structure, systems, and hiring plan a growing organization needs; and sustain our entrepreneurial culture while adding the discipline that growth requires.

Board partnership

Work with the Board on governance, board development, strategy, and fundraising engagement.

Who We're Looking For

We are looking for a confident, entrepreneurial leader who is energized rather than daunted by ambitious goals — someone who can hold their own with a legislator, a corporate government affairs executive, a foundation program officer, and a Tribal leader, sometimes on the same day.

Policy credibility

Demonstrated success in policy advocacy, government affairs, or a closely adjacent arena, and the ability to establish credibility quickly on complex climate and energy issues. Significant climate, energy, or environmental policy experience and familiarity with the Washington political landscape are highly desirable. Deep technical expertise is not required; the ability to be taken seriously by people who have it is.

Revenue generation

A track record of bringing money in the door — through contracts and funded work, corporate sponsorship and membership, earned revenue, government grants, or philanthropy. We are as interested in candidates who have built business development or commercial revenue as in those who have raised money in a nonprofit setting. Aptitude, relationship instinct, and a willingness to ask matter more to us than the sector where you learned it.

Business acumen

Comfort and credibility with corporations and senior business leaders, and an understanding of the commercial, political, and reputational considerations they navigate. Our work sits where business and climate policy meet, and our next leader needs to be effective in both settings.

Entrepreneurial leadership

Experience leading a small, nimble, high-performing team and turning opportunity into results. A background that includes founding, launching, or substantially growing an organization or program is a strong fit, as is the ability to add structure without losing momentum.

Network

A relevant network of policy, business, philanthropic, or civic relationships, or the demonstrated ability to build one quickly. Existing Washington relationships are an advantage rather than a requirement.

Leadership style

Diplomatic, collaborative, and credible. A leader who trusts experts and delegates genuinely, who is willing to have hard conversations with grace, who works from data by instinct, and who cares more about the outcome than the credit.

Prior Executive Director experience is not required

We are more interested in evidence that you can lead a high-performing team, carry an organization's external reputation, and generate revenue than in whether you have held the title before. Strong candidates from business, government, consulting, philanthropy, advocacy, and other senior leadership roles are encouraged to apply.

Compensation, Location, and Benefits

This is a full-time, salaried position with an expected range of $185,000 – $215,000, depending on qualifications and experience.

The role is remote, with regular in-person meetings in the Seattle metro area and travel within Washington and occasionally beyond. Benefits include unlimited paid time off, a Safe Harbor 401(k) matching 100% of the first 5%, and an annual health reimbursement toward coverage you choose.

How to Apply

Online applications only, please — no email or paper submissions. You will be asked to upload a cover letter and resume. In your cover letter, please describe how your experience, interests, and values fit with our mission and the opportunity described here.

Search Timeline: Applications received by October 19, 2026 will receive full consideration; early applications are encouraged. All applicants will receive an email confirmation. Interviewing is anticipated to begin in late October, with additional rounds through November and a hiring decision expected before the end of the year. The desired start date is early January 2027.

Questions regarding this opportunity are welcomed and can be directed to:

Julie Edsforth, julie(at)cloversearchworks.com

Clover Search Works facilitates leadership searches for nonprofit organizations whose missions strengthen communities. Clover is honored to be partnering with Clean & Prosperous in this search.

Job Title

College Admissions Consultant

Job Description

College Admissions Consultants offer personalized, one-on-one guidance to students and families throughout their high school years, helping them confidently navigate the college application and admissions process. This role requires close collaboration with students to develop comprehensive admissions strategies that encompass both academic and extracurricular growth. The College Admissions Consultant will assist students in identifying colleges that align with their academic profiles, career aspirations, and personal preferences. Additionally, they provide expert support in crafting compelling application materials, including essays, resumes, and preparation for interviews.

As a College Admissions Consultant, you will:

  • Conduct individualized strategy sessions with students beginning in 9th grade to evaluate academic performance, extracurricular involvement, career aspirations, and personal goals, driving the creation of tailored college admissions strategies to position students for competitive applications.
  • Maintain consistent communication with students and parents to ensure alignment and clarity around college admissions goals and progress.
  • Conduct in-depth research and analysis for each student to develop a balanced college list, comprising reach, target, and likely schools that align with their academic interests, personal preferences, and family budget.
  • Assist students in brainstorming, outlining, and refining personal statements and supplemental essays to create compelling narratives.
  • Manage application timelines and provide detailed guidance to ensure students complete applications accurately, highlighting their achievements to stand out in the admissions process.
  • Provide expert guidance on course selection, standardized testing (SAT, ACT, etc.), and extracurricular activities that will enhance students' application profiles.
  • Review and optimize student resumes, ensuring they effectively showcase key strengths, experiences, and accomplishments.
  • Prepare students for college interviews by conducting mock interviews and providing constructive feedback for improvement.
  • Stay current on trends in college admissions, including evolving standards and application requirements, to provide the most relevant advice.

Additional responsibilities may be assigned based on the needs of the department and the qualifications of the candidate:

  • Participate in webinars to connect with a wider audience of students and parents, enhancing Kaplan's visibility and establishing the company as a trusted source of information in college consulting.
  • Provide consulting services in curriculum development, counselor training, product strategy, and content creation, ensuring that educational offerings align with industry best practices and effectively meet the needs of students.

You are:

  • An Industry Expert. You bring 5+ years of professional college counseling experience, either at a company or as an independent consultant. You have expert knowledge of the college application process and love to nerd out on industry trends and college admission updates.
  • Enthusiastic. You can captivate any audience with your excitement and your expertise, making you a great communicator.
  • Resourceful. You’re quick, clever, and solution-oriented. You can take information and run with it - you don’t rely on a lot of direction. You’re comfortable working online with students and learning new systems.
  • Self-Motivated. You’re adept at working independently and can manage your time efficiently.
  • Passionate. When you work with students, it’s clear that you’re invested in their journey.

Requirements

  • Bachelor's degree

  • Extensive knowledge of the college application process, including admissions requirements, financial aid, scholarship opportunities, and academic planning
  • Strong communication, presentation, and meeting facilitation skills
  • Exceptional writing skills to communicate effectively with students and families and navigate the essay editing process
  • Excellent organizational skills and the ability to manage multiple students and track their progress through the application cycle simultaneously

Preferred Requirements

  • Masters degree in counseling, higher education, or similar
  • Strong experience helping multiple students get accepted to highly selective schools
  • Experience working in college admissions, preferably at a highly selective institution
  • International admissions experience
  • Must be authorized to work in the United States

The salary rate for one-on-one advising starts at $100 an hour. Actual compensation for this role is determined by several factors including but not limited to job level, candidate's skills, experience, and education, among other factors determined by the business.

Job Title: Marketing Events Manager

Location: New York, NY, Atlanta, GA, or Remote, USA

Exemption Status: Full-time, exempt

Who We Are

Impiricus is the Agentic Commercialization Platform for Healthcare. We help life sciences teams understand physician intent, coordinate the right clinical and commercial resources, and enable real-time action when HCPs need support. Our AI-powered platform acts as a field force multiplier: extending reach between rep visits, prioritizing the highest-impact path for each physician, and connecting HCPs to coverage, evidence, medical information, patient support, MSLs, field teams, samples, and approved content in the moments that matter.

Founded by a practicing physician and a senior pharmaceutical executive, Impiricus was built to accelerate patient access to life-saving treatments through ethical, physician-first engagement. More than one million opted-in HCPs trust Impiricus as a preferred channel, including many who are underserved or hard to reach through traditional outreach. Products such as the Intelligently Optimized Network (ION), Pulse, Spark, and Ascend work together so every interaction can move from information to action. Guided by our Physician Advisory Board, we keep engagement clinically meaningful, compliant, and grounded in better patient care.

Job Summary:

The Marketing Events Manager will play a key role in elevating the Impiricus brand through the planning and execution of high-impact pharma and industry conferences, sponsorships, and client-facing experiences. This role will own end-to-end execution across key event programs, including thought leadership opportunities, roundtables, executive dinners, and other sponsorship activations designed to strengthen client relationships and create meaningful opportunities for the Sales team.

You’ll collaborate closely with Marketing, Sales, leadership, and external partners to ensure every event is thoughtfully planned, executed seamlessly, and aligned with broader commercial priorities. From managing sponsorship deliverables and event logistics to coordinating speakers, meetings, travel, and onsite execution, you’ll help turn event strategy into experiences that drive visibility, engagement, and business impact.

This is an ideal opportunity for a highly organized, proactive, and resourceful marketer who thrives in fast-paced environments, enjoys cross-functional collaboration, and can confidently manage multiple high-priority events from planning through execution.

Responsibilities:

Event Execution

  • Oversee end-to-end planning of assigned pharma and industry conferences including managing timelines, operations/logistics, budgets, and booth/sponsorship deliverables.
  • Own fulfillment of all sponsorship deliverables including registrations, tabletop booth displays, branding/creative assets, and other contracted benefits.
  • Plan and execute roundtables and client dinners, including venue/vendor coordination, guest list development, attendee recruitment communications, and other event deliverables.
  • Manage on-site presence, as needed - ensuring everything runs smoothly and reflects the Impiricus standard of excellence.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Work closely with sales and commercial leaders to coordinate priority attendees, client meetings, networking opportunities and event follow ups.
  • Partner with marketing and design leaders to coordinate event content, marketing collateral and social media engagement.
  • Serve as the primary operational liaison with conference organizers, vendors, and other external event stakeholders.

Performance Measurement

  • Ensure event leads, meetings, attendance and engagement data are accurately captured and shared with sales and marketing for timely follow up.
  • Maintain documentation, timelines, and processes for scalable event management practices.
  • Communicate roadblocks and program updates in a timely and effective fashion.

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Marketing, Communications, Business, or a related field.
  • 4+ years of experience in event marketing, conference management, or corporate event management - ideally within pharma, healthcare, technology, or SaaS industries.
  • Proven success managing multiple complex events, sponsorships, and event programs simultaneously.
  • Strong project management skills and high attention to detail.
  • Experience using project management, marketing and event tools (Asana, Cvent, Hubspot, etc.)
  • Excellent communication and collaboration skills, with experience managing vendors, external partners, and cross-functional stakeholders.
  • Comfortable working in a dynamic, remote-first environment.
  • Ability and willingness to travel for onsite event execution and support.

Compensation and Benefits

The base salary for this role is $95,000 - $115,000.

Where you land within the range will reflect your skills, experience, and location, while keeping team parity in mind and leaving room for future growth.

Important Notice

To protect candidates, please note that all communication from our team will come directly from an @impiricus.com email address. We do not engage third party recruiters to schedule interviews for this role. If you receive outreach from anyone outside of our domain claiming to represent Impiricus, please disregard and let us know by forwarding the message to

Benefits:

Impiricus focuses on taking care of our teammates’ professional and personal growth and well-being.

Healthcare: Medical, dental, and vision coverage for you and your dependents + on-demand healthcare concierge
HSA, FSA & DCFSA: Pre-tax savings options for healthcare and dependent care, with monthly employer contributions to HSA (if enrolled in a high-deductible plan)
Coverage & Protection: 100% paid short- and long-term disability, plus life and AD&D insurance
Flexible Time Off: Take the time you need with a flexible vacation policy — recharge your batteries your way
Parental Leave: Paid parental leave to spend time with your newborn, adopted, or foster child (available after 6 months)
Your Work, Your Way: If you’re close to an office, we encourage spending some time in-person to collaborate and connect. If not, remote is always an option.
401(k): Save for your future with tax advantages (and company match!)

Impiricus provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Join the remote team of one of the fastest-growing boutique law firms in the Washington, DC area.

PJI Law, PLC is a boutique, service-focused law firm committed to delivering exceptional client experiences. Every conversation matters, and our Intake Specialists play a critical role in helping people during some of the most important moments of their lives.

We're looking for high-performing sales professionals who thrive on helping people, consistently exceed goals, embrace accountability, and are motivated by uncapped earning potential.

This is not a traditional call center or customer service role. It is a consultative sales position where your ability to build trust, qualify prospective clients, and confidently guide them toward the right consultation directly impacts your success.

No legal industry experience? No problem. We provide comprehensive subject matter and sales training. What we need you to bring is drive, resilience, coachability, and the desire to win.

$1,784 USD per month

Why PJI Law?

Our vision is to elevate the standard for legal services everywhere we go.

Our mission is to ensure everyone who contacts our firm walks away with more peace of mind, a brighter future, and a bigger smile.

We live by three core values:

  • Professionalism
  • Excellence
  • Integrity

We're proud to have earned the Great Place to Work® Certification every year since 2022, reflecting our commitment to building an environment where exceptional people can do their best work.

If you're looking for more than just another remote sales job and want to join a team that invests in your success while rewarding high performance, we'd love to hear from you.

raw.description:
About Us

BRIGHTSCOUT is a global B2B branding and development agency specializing in elevating emerging tech businesses through uniquely crafted brands and standout apps. Comprised of top-tier talent worldwide, we offer a powerful blend of exquisite design, robust development, and strategic acumen. More than a company, BRIGHTSCOUT is a tribe dedicated to disrupting the tech industry with bold ideas and collaborative genius.

The Role

As a Technical Product Manager at BRIGHTSCOUT, you'll decide what gets built and why, then make sure it actually ships. On accounts where the client has their own product team, you'll partner with them to translate their vision into a backlog our engineering and design teams can execute against. On accounts where they don't, you'll be that product team: setting direction, making the calls a client's own PM would make, and representing their business goals inside every planning conversation.

This is a hybrid role by design. Some weeks you're closer to a Product Manager, working the vision, roadmap, and stakeholder tradeoffs. Other weeks you're closer to a Product Owner, writing acceptance criteria and keeping a sprint on track. You'll move fluidly between the two, and know which one a given moment calls for.

Responsibilities

  • Product Vision, Client Partnership & Backlog Ownership
  • Act as the acting product lead for clients without an in-house PM, building a working command of their business, users, and market deep enough to make credible calls on their behalf.
  • Translate ambiguous business goals and stakeholder input into a clear product vision, roadmap, and prioritized, sequenced backlog — grooming it by user value, dependency, risk, and effort.
  • Run or support discovery and requirements gathering alongside our Solutions and Delivery teams, turning findings into epics, user stories, and acceptance criteria the team can execute against.
  • Represent the client's product interests in internal planning, and represent technical and delivery realities back to the client, in both directions; present roadmaps, tradeoffs, and progress in plain language, holding the line on scope when priorities exceed what a sprint or budget can support.
  • Review completed work against acceptance criteria and accept it into the baseline — you're the team's quality gate for whether the work meets the intent, not just the ticket.

Agile Execution, Collaboration & Tooling

  • Run or co-run agile ceremonies (standups, sprint planning, reviews, retros), keeping the team anchored to sprint and release goals.
  • Partner daily with design, engineering, and QA to resolve ambiguity and keep tradeoffs visible to the business side.
  • Work alongside our Project Management team on scope, risk, and budget: you own what gets built, they own the plan and the day-to-day client cadence, and the two of you keep each other honest. Coordinate with the shared Capabilities team to keep priorities aligned across concurrent engagements.
  • Use AI-assisted tools for research synthesis, spec drafting, and backlog grooming, with the judgment to know when to override a first draft.
  • Stay fluent in modern product and delivery tooling (Jira, Linear, Notion, Productboard, or equivalent) and comfortable enough with Figma to work directly with designers.

Requirements

  • 5+ years of experience spanning product management and product ownership, ideally including agency, consultancy, or client-services work — comfortable owning both ends of the job, from setting direction with a client to writing a precise acceptance criterion.
  • Enough technical fluency to hold a real conversation with engineers about architecture tradeoffs, APIs, and technical debt, without needing to write the code yourself.
  • Analytically minded and hypothesis-driven, comfortable making calls with incomplete information, with a genuine sense of ownership over outcomes, not just outputs.
  • Strong written and verbal communication, able to translate technical constraints for a client and business goals for a dev team, in both directions.
  • Practical, hands-on experience with Agile/Scrum, modern delivery tooling, and AI tools for research, writing, and backlog work.

Our Values

  • Lead with Heart: We build honest, trusting relationships and care for each other.
  • Break Convention: We seek bold ideas, we transform fearless creativity into tangible results.
  • Bring Order to the Chaos: We transform complexity into clarity.
  • Be a Champion: We strive for excellence.

Why Us

  • Unlimited PTO: Enjoy a truly flexible work-life balance with our unlimited paid time off policy. Take the time you need to recharge and perform at your best.
  • Remote Work: Work from anywhere! We embrace remote work, giving you the freedom to choose your ideal work environment.
  • Flexible Schedule Tied To Project Needs: We understand that life happens. Our flexible schedules, aligned with project milestones, allow you to manage your time effectively and achieve your best results.
  • Salary in USD: Receive competitive compensation in USD.

Interview Process

  1. Resume Review by Talent Team.
  2. Screening Interview by Talent Team.
  3. Interview w/ Hiring Manager and Delivery Manager
  4. Assessment/Technical Challenge
  5. Interview w/ Co-Founders
  6. Final Selection and Offer.

Ready to Elevate your Career at BRIGHTSCOUT?

At BRIGHTSCOUT, we value more than skills and experience; we seek individuals who embody kindness, empathy, and collaboration in their work. We believe these qualities contribute to the team and the company's overall success.

BRIGHTSCOUT is an equal opportunity employer and values diversity. We prohibit discrimination and harassment based on race, religion, color, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status. We are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees and encourage all qualified candidates to apply.
